title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Longue Marche, 2nd part, p.305 in Grothendieck's own numbering). Γ is a subgroup of Autext_lac(π̂_{0,3}) commuting with S_3, a GT-type group containing the image of Gal(Q̄/Q). N_{1,1} is the corresponding extension of Γ by the profinite genus-1 mapping class group Γ̂_{1,1} ≅ SL(2,Z)^ (profinite completion), modelled on the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1} over Q. The target is the homomorphism (21) N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ), the 'Tate-module' representation, i.e. the action on H_1 of the once-punctured torus ⊗ Ẑ.

On the previous page he obtained weaker versions of (21). First, φ: N_{1,1} → GP(1,Ẑ) = PGL(2,Ẑ), from the outer action. Second, the cyclotomic character χ (the determinant). Together these give ψ: N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ)/₂Ẑ*, where ₂Ẑ* = {λ : λ²=1} ≅ (Z/2)^P is the kernel of u ↦ (ū, det u).

On this page:
(i) ψ kills the central element −1 (the elliptic involution). So it factors as Ψ': N'_{1,1} = N_{1,1}/±1 → GL(2,Ẑ)/₂Ẑ* (display (32), labelled (31) on the sheet). Here N'_{1,1} is an extension of Γ by Γ̂'_{1,1} ≅ Ŝ⁺_{0,3}, the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z) = (Γ(2)/±1) ⋊ S_3, an extension of S_3 by π̂_{0,3}.
(ii) Ψ' should be constructible directly from N'_{1,1}, exactly as ψ was. Conjugation gives N'_{1,1} → Aut(Ŝ⁺_{0,3}), and one passes to the congruence quotient PSL(2,Ẑ) = SL(2,Ẑ)'. For this one only needs the canonical map GP(1,Ẑ) ≅ GL(2,Ẑ)/Ẑ* → Aut(SL(2,Ẑ)') (33) to be injective. It is: conjugation by PGL(2,Z_p) on PSL(2,Z_p) has trivial centralizer.
(iii) The essential open question is to make explicit the lift of Ψ' to (34) N'_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ)' := GL(2,Ẑ)/±1. Once that is done, N_{1,1} is recovered as the pull-back of the central extension (35) 1→{±1}→GL(2,Ẑ)→GL(2,Ẑ)'→1, together with (21). The aim is to reconstruct the genus-1 level (the central Z/2 of the elliptic involution and the Tate representation) purely from genus-0 data, namely Γ acting on π̂_{0,3} with S_3-symmetry.

The lifting problem amounts to choosing coherently a sign in each p-component of ₂Ẑ*/±1 ≅ (Z/2)^P/diag. Lifts form a torsor under Hom(N'_{1,1}, (Z/2)^P/±1) once the obstruction vanishes. The next page confirms this is 'la question essentielle'.
errors: The marginal insertion 'Ŝ⁺_{0,3} ≃ Sl(2,Ẑ)′' identifies the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z) with PSL(2,Ẑ). This is false: SL(2,Z) lacks the congruence subgroup property, so the map PSL(2,Z)^ → PSL(2,Ẑ) is surjective with a huge (free profinite) kernel. Grothendieck corrects this on the next page, writing SL(2,Z)'^∧ and the arrow (38) Ŝ⁺_{0,3} → SL(2,Ẑ)'.

Implicit gap: the 'direct' construction of Ψ' needs the action of N'_{1,1} on Ŝ⁺_{0,3} to preserve the congruence kernel. This holds for the Galois image (level structures are defined over Q(μ_n)) but is not argued for a general Γ.
The second display is labelled (31) again; the next page calls it (32).

ideas.what: Factorization of the weakened Tate representation through the quotient by the elliptic involution, N_{1,1}/±1 = extension of Γ by PSL(2,Z)^ ≅ Ŝ⁺_{0,3} (genus-1 level seen as an S_3-extension of the genus-0 group)
ideas.modern_name: GT/Galois action on Γ̂_{1,1} and \hat B_3 via the Legendre/λ-line (M_{0,4}→M_{1,1}) description; PSL(2,Z) ≅ F_2 ⋊ S_3
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the modular tower and reconstruction from genus 0 and 1 in general terms only

ideas.what: Injectivity of PGL(2,Ẑ) → Aut(PSL(2,Ẑ)) used to recover a projective Tate representation from the conjugation action
ideas.modern_name: trivial centralizer / automorphisms of PSL_2 over Z_p

ideas.what: Lifting problem: from N'_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ)/₂Ẑ* to N'_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ)/±1, then recovering N_{1,1} and (21) by pull-back of the central extension by ±1
ideas.modern_name: lifting through central extension by (Z/2)^P; Galois image of the Tate module of the universal elliptic curve at a tangential base point (diag(χ,1))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura, Ihara–Matsumoto, Hain–Matsumoto for the Galois case

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, but does not solve, the problem of canonically lifting the GT-type action from the ±1-quotient to the full genus-1 extension. The point is to obtain the Tate representation N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ) from genus-0 data alone, for an arbitrary Γ ⊂ Autext_lac(π̂_{0,3}) commuting with S_3. For Gal(Q̄/Q), or GT acting via a tangential base point, the answer is essentially known in the later literature (diagonal action via χ). The general abstract version, i.e. an obstruction in H² with (Z/2)^P coefficients for arbitrary such Γ, does not seem to be treated explicitly.
missed.quote: La question se pose ici (question que je n'ai pas pu préciser...) comment expliciter le relèvement de Ψ' de (31) en l'homom. canonique (34) N'_{1,1} → Gl(2,Ẑ)' = Gl(2,Ẑ)/±1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to whether genus-1 data (and the elliptic involution's central extension) is determined by genus-0 data for subgroups of GT, which is close to the Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps 'new version of GT' discussion. The specific (Z/2)^P sign-lifting formulation is a minor but concrete point.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working step in the well-known programme of making GT/Galois act on genus-1 mapping class groups via genus 0. That theme was developed later by Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps and Hain–Matsumoto. The explicit lifting question is a nice detail, but it is largely resolved in the Galois case by tangential base points, and it contains a congruence-completion slip that he fixes on the next page.
transcription_corrections: In (33), 'Gl(1,Ẑ)' should be 'GP(1,Ẑ)' (projective linear group = GL(2,Ẑ)/Ẑ*), as the vertical ≃ to Gl(2,Ẑ)/Ẑ* shows.
'Aut_ext' in (33) is likely 'Aut_lac' (compare (36) on the next page), or plain Aut as in (37).
The second display labelled '(31)' is (32) according to the next page ('relèvement (34) de (32)').
'Γ^{±'}_{1,1}' is probably 'Γ^{+'}_{1,1}' (the ±1-quotient of Γ̂_{1,1}); 'Π_Q' is probably Γ_Q or Γ.
